items.zh: 三三昧 · 釋名 · 辯相 · 出生三昧

zh: 次釋三三昧。三三昧者：一、有覺有觀三昧；二、無覺有觀三昧；三、無覺無觀三昧。所以次九定後明三三昧者，此二種禪，名雖有異，而法相孱同。所以者何？九定既通鍊諸禪，而自無別體。三三昧亦如是，此義在下自當可見。釋三三昧，即為三意：一、釋名；二、辯相；三、名出生三昧。
en: Next, explaining the three samādhis. The three samādhis are: first, the samādhi possessing initial thought and sustained reflection; second, the samādhi without initial thought but possessing sustained reflection; third, the samādhi without either initial thought or sustained reflection. As for why the three samādhis are explained here, following the nine sequential concentrations: though these two kinds of dhyāna differ in name, their own dharma-marks are closely alike. Why is this? The nine concentrations, already universally refining every dhyāna, possess no separate substance of their own; the three samādhis, too, are just the same — this sense may be seen for itself below.
Explaining the three samādhis now has three senses: first, explaining the name; second, distinguishing their mark; third, naming the samādhis they give rise to.

zh: 第一、釋名。覺觀等三法，名同次位，已如前根本禪中說，三昧今當分別。一切禪定攝心，皆名為三摩提，秦言正心行處。是心從無始已來，常曲不端，得是正心行處，心則端直，故名三昧。譬如蛇行常曲，入筒則直。此亦如是。問曰：若言禪定攝心名三昧者，根本禪定與此有何異？答曰：有異。彼則但明根本攝心，今遍約一切諸禪中明攝心當如此，則定深而廣，豈得不異？復次，根本禪但是緣事攝心，未斷邪倒，不名端直。今明三昧，並據緣理攝心，能斷邪倒之曲，故以心端直處為三昧也。
en: First, explaining the name: the three dharmas of initial thought, sustained reflection, and the rest, their name matching their own sequence of stages, have already been explained above, within the root dhyānas; samādhi shall now be distinguished. Every dhyāna concentration that gathers in the mind is, in general, named samādhi — in the language of the Qin, "the place where the mind moves correctly." This mind, ever since beginningless time, has constantly been crooked and never upright; obtaining this very place where the mind moves correctly, the mind thereby becomes upright and straight — hence this is named samādhi. It is like a snake, whose movement is always crooked, entering a bamboo tube and thereby made straight — this, too, is just the same.

Question: should one say that dhyāna concentration gathering in the mind is named samādhi, how, then, does this differ from the root dhyāna concentrations themselves? Answer: there is a difference. Those explain only the gathering of the mind within the root dhyānas; here, it is clarified, universally, with reference to gathering the mind within every dhyāna — this being so, the concentration is both deep and broad — how could it not differ? Furthermore, the root dhyānas merely gather the mind by taking concrete phenomena as their object, not yet severing the crookedness of wrong views, and thus are not named upright and straight. Here, clarifying samādhi, this is, in every case, based upon gathering the mind by taking principle itself as the object, able to sever the very crookedness of wrong views — hence the place where the mind is upright and straight is named samādhi.

zh: 第二、次辯相者，此三三昧義同九定，既無別體，但約諸禪以辯相也。一、明有覺三昧，如上所說根本初禪乃至特勝、通明、背捨、勝處等初禪，各有覺有觀相應心數及諸功德。行者入此等諸初禪時，住正心行處，皆名有覺有觀三昧。二、如上所說諸禪中間乃至特勝、通明、背捨、勝處，各有中間與觀相應心數法及諸功德。行者以正心行處入此等諸禪中間，皆名無覺有觀三昧。三、如上所說根本二禪乃至有頂及特勝、通明、背捨、勝處等，各有二禪，從二禪已去，乃至有頂及滅受想定，有無覺無觀相應法并諸功德。行者正心行處，入此等諸禪功德，皆名無覺無觀三昧。
en: Second, next distinguishing their mark: the sense of these three samādhis is identical to that of the nine concentrations, possessing no separate substance of their own, and are distinguished in their mark solely with reference to the various dhyānas themselves.

First, clarifying the samādhi possessing initial thought: as already explained above, the root first dhyāna, and, further still, the first dhyāna belonging to the special excellences, the thorough-and-bright contemplation, detachment, and the stations of mastery, each, alike, possess initial thought and sustained reflection, their own corresponding mental factors, and every merit belonging to them. The practitioner, entering these various first dhyānas, abiding in the place where the mind moves correctly — this is, in every case, named the samādhi possessing initial thought and sustained reflection.

Second, as already explained above, the various dhyānas' own intermediate stage, and, further still, the intermediate stage belonging to the special excellences, the thorough-and-bright contemplation, detachment, and the stations of mastery, each, alike, possess an intermediate stage together with sustained reflection's own corresponding mental factors and every merit belonging to them. The practitioner, through the place where the mind moves correctly, entering these various intermediate stages — this is, in every case, named the samādhi without initial thought but possessing sustained reflection.

Third, as already explained above, the root second dhyāna, and, further still, up through the peak of existence, together with the second dhyāna belonging to the special excellences, the thorough-and-bright contemplation, detachment, and the stations of mastery — from the second dhyāna onward, all the way through the peak of existence and the concentration of the cessation of sensation and perception, there is present the dharma corresponding to neither initial thought nor sustained reflection, together with every merit belonging to it. The practitioner, through the place where the mind moves correctly, entering these various dhyānas' own merit — this is, in every case, named the samādhi without either initial thought or sustained reflection.

zh: 當知此三三昧更無別體，但是總諸禪以為三分。大聖欲令眾生雖聞廣說諸禪，而不失根本故，總以三法收攝諸禪，罄無不盡。譬如數法，若至百萬，總為一億，此亦如是。第三、明出生三昧之相者，則有二種：一者、出生二乘三昧。所以者何？如上所說，諸有覺有觀初禪等，悉發念處三昧，乃至八聖道、空、無相、無作、十六行、十二因緣、暖、頂、忍、世第一等三昧、電光三昧、金剛三昧乃至佛智無諍等三昧。此諸法門，《涅槃經》中悉說名三昧也。若於諸初禪中發此等三昧，即證二乘若道若果，故名有覺有觀三昧。乃至無覺有觀、無覺無觀，亦當如是一一分別。
en: One should know, then, that these three samādhis possess no separate substance of their own whatsoever, but are simply every dhyāna gathered together and divided into three portions. The great sage, wishing to ensure that sentient beings, though hearing every dhyāna explained at length, would not lose sight of the root, therefore gathered in every dhyāna, in general, through these three dharmas, leaving nothing whatsoever uncovered — like the method of counting: reaching a million, one gathers this, in general, into a single yi (here, the unit equal to a million); this, too, is just the same.

Third, clarifying the mark of the samādhis these three give rise to: this is of two kinds. First, giving rise to the two vehicles' own samādhis. Why is this? As already explained above, the various first dhyānas possessing initial thought and sustained reflection all give rise to the samādhi of the foundations of mindfulness, and, further still, the eight-fold noble path, emptiness, signlessness, no-action, the sixteen practices, the twelve links of dependent origination, the samādhis of heat, summit, forbearance, and the supreme mundane dharma, the lightning-flash samādhi, the vajra samādhi, and, further still, the buddha-wisdom's own samādhi free of contention and the rest. These very dharma-gates are, throughout the Nirvāṇa Sūtra, in every case, spoken of and named samādhis. Should one, within these various first dhyānas, give rise to samādhis such as these, one thereby realizes the path or the fruit belonging to the two vehicles — hence this is named the samādhi possessing initial thought and sustained reflection. And, further still, the samādhi without initial thought but possessing sustained reflection, and the samādhi without either, should each, in turn, be distinguished in this same way.

zh: 二者、如上所說諸有覺有觀禪各發大乘諸三昧者，如觀佛三昧、二十五三昧、般舟三昧、首楞嚴等諸菩薩三昧，百則有八，諸佛三昧不動等，百則有二十及八萬四千諸三昧等，皆因有覺有觀三昧發。乃至無覺有觀、無覺無觀，亦當如是一一分別。菩薩摩訶薩得此諸三昧故，即入菩薩位，亦能現身，如佛度一切眾生。三三昧義，如《摩訶衍》中廣分別。
en: Second, as already explained above, the various dhyānas possessing initial thought and sustained reflection each also give rise to the Mahāyāna's own samādhis — such as the samādhi of buddha-contemplation, the twenty-five samādhis, the pratyutpanna samādhi, the Śūraṅgama samādhi, and every other bodhisattva samādhi, a full hundred and eight in number; and the buddhas' own samādhis, the unmoving and the rest, a full hundred and twenty, together with the eighty-four thousand samādhis and the rest — all, alike, arising through the samādhi possessing initial thought and sustained reflection. And, further still, the samādhi without initial thought but possessing sustained reflection, and the samādhi without either, should each, in turn, be distinguished in this same way.

The bodhisattva-mahāsattva, having obtained these samādhis, thereupon enters the bodhisattva's own stage, and is also able to manifest the body, delivering every sentient being across, just as the Buddha himself does. The sense of the three samādhis is explained at greater length in the Mahāyāna treatise.

The etymology offered for samādhi — "the place where the mind moves correctly," a naturally crooked mind straightened the way a snake is straightened by entering a bamboo tube — is one of this treatise's more vivid images for what concentration actually does to an untrained mind. The chapter's real payoff, though, is structural: the three samādhis are explicitly declared to have "no separate substance of their own," merely the entire preceding catalog of dhyānas sorted into three bins by whether initial thought and sustained reflection are present, absent-but-partial, or absent entirely — the "reaching a million, gathered into a single yi" simile makes the point that this is a classification scheme, not a ninth or tenth new practice. The scale of what these three samādhis are said to give rise to — over a hundred named Mahāyāna samādhis, eighty-four thousand more besides — closes the "observational gates" material (detachment, mastery, totality, sequential concentration) on the largest possible register before the fascicle's final two, most virtuosic samādhis.

zh: 次釋師子奮迅三昧。今明師子奮迅三昧者，如《般若經》中說，行者依九次第定入師子奮迅三昧。云何名師子三昧？離欲，離不善法，有覺有觀，離生喜樂，入初禪，如是次第入二禪、三禪、四禪、空處、識處、不用處、非有想非無想處，入滅受想定，從滅受想定起，還入非有想非無想定，從非有想非無想處起，還入不用處，如是次第，還入識處，入空處，入四禪，入三禪，入二禪，入初禪，是名師子奮迅三昧也。
en: Next, explaining the lion's-frolic samādhi. Here, clarifying the lion's-frolic samādhi: as explained in the Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, the practitioner, based upon the nine sequential concentrations, enters the lion's-frolic samādhi. What is meant by the lion's samādhi? Departing from desire, departing from unwholesome dharmas, possessing initial thought and sustained reflection, with joy and happiness born of separation, entering the first dhyāna; and, in this same sequence, entering the second dhyāna, the third dhyāna, the fourth dhyāna, the sphere of space, the sphere of consciousness, the sphere of nothingness, and the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, entering the concentration of the cessation of sensation and perception; then, rising from the concentration of the cessation of sensation and perception, entering back into the concentration of neither-perception-nor-non-perception; rising from the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, entering back into the sphere of nothingness; and so, in this same sequence, entering back into the sphere of consciousness, entering the sphere of space, entering the fourth dhyāna, entering the third dhyāna, entering the second dhyāna, entering the first dhyāna — this is named the lion's-frolic samādhi.

zh: 譬如師子奮迅之時，非但能前進奮迅而去，亦能却行奮迅而歸，一切諸獸所不能爾。行者入此法門亦復如是，非但能心心次第從於初禪，直至滅受，亦能從滅受想定却入非想，入至初禪。此則義同師子奮迅，上來諸禪所不能爾，故說此定為師子奮迅三昧。行者住此法門，即能覆却，遍入一切諸禪，熏諸觀定，悉令通利，轉變自在，出生諸深三昧種種功德，神智轉勝，亦名熏禪。譬如牛皮熏熟，隨意作諸世物。此亦如是。分別次位，此同九定，但有却出無間之異。是中用心巧細修習之相，略知大意，不廣分別也。
en: It is like the lion, at the moment of its own frolicking leap, not merely able to bound forward in its leap, but also able to leap backward in its return — something no other beast whatsoever is able to do. The practitioner, entering this dharma-gate, is likewise so: not merely able, mind following mind in sequence, to proceed from the first dhyāna directly through to the cessation of sensation, but also able, from the concentration of the cessation of sensation and perception, to turn back and enter neither-perception-nor-non-perception, all the way back to the first dhyāna. This, then, is identical in sense to the lion's own frolicking leap, something none of the dhyānas given above were able to do — hence this concentration is named the lion's-frolic samādhi.

The practitioner, abiding within this dharma-gate, is thereby able to turn back and forth, entering every dhyāna throughout completely, permeating every contemplative concentration, causing them all to flow freely, transforming at will, giving rise to every kind of merit belonging to the deepest samādhis, spiritual wisdom growing ever more excellent — also named the permeating dhyāna. It is like an ox-hide, once thoroughly permeated and softened, able to be fashioned into any worldly object at will — this, too, is just the same. Distinguishing its own stage, this is identical to the nine concentrations, differing only in its own turning back and forth without any interval. The skillful and fine application of the mind's own cultivation here is, in brief, known in its general sense, and not distinguished at greater length.

The lion's-frolic samādhi's defining move — not just ascending through all nine sequential concentrations, but reversing direction at the very peak and descending back through them in the same unbroken sequence — earns its name from a lion's own unique capacity, unlike every other beast, to leap backward as fluidly as forward. This is the treatise's clearest image yet for what "permeating" (熏) means as distinct from "refining" (鍊): refining makes each individual stage purer in isolation, like tempering metal, while permeating works the entire sequence bidirectionally until it is uniformly pliant throughout, like an ox-hide worked until it can be shaped into anything at all.

options: with thought and reflection; without thought but with reflection; without either
quiz.why: They are the samādhi with thought and reflection, without thought but with reflection, and without either.

quiz.q: How is samādhi rendered in Chinese, and what simile is used?
options: "the place where the mind moves correctly"; the crooked mind made straight, like a snake entering a tube
quiz.why: Samādhi is rendered "the place where the mind moves correctly"; the mind, crooked since beginningless time, is made straight, like a snake straightened in a bamboo tube.

quiz.q: How does this samādhi differ from the root dhyānas' gathering of the mind?
options: the root gathers the mind on phenomena without severing crookedness; this gathers it on principle, severing it
quiz.why: The root dhyānas gather the mind on phenomena without severing wrong views; this samādhi gathers it on principle, severing crookedness.

quiz.q: Which statement about the Mahāyāna samādhis arising from the three is correct?
options: the 108 bodhisattva samādhis, 120 buddha samādhis, and 84,000 all arise from the samādhi with thought and reflection
quiz.why: The bodhisattva samādhis, 108 in number, the buddhas' 120, and the 84,000 all arise through the samādhi with thought and reflection.

quiz.q: Why is the lion's-frolic samādhi so named?
options: the lion leaps forward and back; the practitioner goes up to cessation and back down to the first dhyāna
quiz.why: As a lion leaps forward and backward, the practitioner passes in order up to cessation and back down to the first dhyāna. Skipping stages is transcendence.

quiz.q: Why is it also called the permeating dhyāna, and with what simile?
options: it permeates every dhyāna making them supple, like cured ox-hide shaped into anything
quiz.why: Turning back and forth through every dhyāna, it permeates them so they flow freely, like an ox-hide cured soft and fashioned into anything.
